newsitem.title: BURMA: Burma re-opens access to road near Suu Kyi's home.
newsitem.headline: Burma re-opens access to road near Suu Kyi's home.

text.p: Burmese authorities on Tuesday removed police checkpoints set up nearly two weeks ago to bar public access to opposition leader Aung San Suu Kyi's residence in the capital, witnesses said.

The blockade of University Avenue along which Suu Kyi's home is located began on September 27 as part of efforts by the military government to prevent her from holding a congress of her National League for Democracy (NLD) party.
The State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC) also detained 573 NLD members and supporters before the planned congress from September 27-29.

Late on Monday, a Burmese government official said that only 63 of the detainees were still being held and they were expected to be freed soon. Suu Kyi had disputed the numbers and said up to 800 party activists might have been held in the crackdown.
The road block, originally said by Burma police to be for only a few days, prevented Suu Kyi from holding her usual public gatherings in front of her house for two consecutive weekends.
Repeated attempts to reach Suu Kyi by telephone at her house for comment on the removal of the checkpoints were unsuccessful.
There was also no official comment from the SLORC.
Burma's action against the Suu Kyi and NLD supporters drew condemnation from the United States, Britain and international human rights groups.
U.S. President Bill Clinton responded to the Burmese action by barring entry of Burmese military government officials and members of their family to the United States.
Rangoon reacted by restricting visas to certain categories of U.S. citizens.
